title: Finite free coefficient extensions and cofinal levels
statement:
Fix the global datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ and $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. A coefficient field means a finite extension of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, with its valuation ring and chosen uniformizer [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X,T,Z$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes, let $f:T\to X$ be a separated finite-type morphism, and let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Work first on the ordinary small etale derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Bounded constructible means [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]; finite Tor amplitude means that for some integers $a\le b$, $\mathcal H^r(K\otimes_A^L N)=0$ for every degree-zero module sheaf $N$ and every $r\notin[a,b]$. On the finite-coefficient pro-etale constructible realization use [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Coefficient extension is the derived change of rings [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Direct image is the usual derived direct image, $Ri_A^!$ on the etale site is the right adjoint of $i_*$ [lem-exc-closed-ambient], and $\omega_{X,A}=a_{X,A}^{\times}A$ with $a_X:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, where $a_{X,A}^{\times}$ is the etale compact-support right adjoint [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint, def-amb-etale-compact-support]. Put $D_{X,A}K=R\mathcal Hom_A(K,\omega_{X,A})$ using [def-pur-derived-internal-hom, lem-weil-duality-pairing]. On the pro-etale realization use the transported exceptional functor and dualizing object [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image, lem-weil-finite-duality-site-comparison]. All tensor products below are derived; since $B$ will be finite free over $A$, tensoring with $B$ is also ordinary exact tensoring. In the direct-image formula $K\in D^b_{ctf}(T,A)$; in the closed-exceptional formula $M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$; in the remaining formulas $K,M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$.

Let $E\subset L$ be a finite extension of coefficient fields,
with ramification index $e$. For every $n\geq1$, put

$$
A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n,\qquad
B=\mathcal O_L/\varpi_E^n\mathcal O_L
=\mathcal O_L/\varpi_L^{en}=A_{L,en}.
$$

Equality here is equality of ideals; a unit relating the chosen
uniformizers does not change the quotient. The coefficient ring
$B$ is finite free over $A$. For finite-Tor constructible
complexes the canonical maps give isomorphisms

$$
\begin{aligned}
(Rf_{*,A}K)\otimes_A B&\cong Rf_{*,B}(K\otimes_A B),\\
(Ri_A^!M)\otimes_A B&\cong Ri_B^!(M\otimes_A B),\\
\omega_{X,A}\otimes_A B&\cong\omega_{X,B},\\
R\mathcal Hom_A(K,M)\otimes_A B
&\cong R\mathcal Hom_B(K\otimes_A B,M\otimes_A B),\\
(D_{X,A}K)\otimes_A B&\cong D_{X,B}(K\otimes_A B).
\end{aligned}
$$

They respect evaluation, double-dual maps and the adjunction
counits, are compatible with further finite coefficient-field
extension, and commute with coefficient reduction. Their formation
is natural under scheme isomorphisms, in particular Frobenius.
Thus the levels $en$ give the coefficient comparisons on a
cofinal subsystem of the $\mathcal O_L$-adic tower.

More explicitly, the direct-image map is the projection comparison [def-kun-projection-formula-map]. The closed-exceptional map is the adjoint of scalar-extended exceptional counit. The dualizing map is adjoint to the scalar-extended compact-support counit using the finite-free comparison $T_{A,B}Ra_{X,A!}\cong Ra_{X,B!}T_{A,B}$, where $T_{A,B}=-\otimes_A^LB$. The internal-Hom map is the transpose of scalar-extended evaluation, and the Verdier map is its composite with the dualizing map. Coefficient-reduction compatibility means the commuting squares for $A_{E,n}\to A_{E,m}$ and $A_{L,en}\to A_{L,em}$, $1\le m\le n$, using the canonical derived tensor reassociations and the quotient comparisons of [lem-coef-finite-direct-image, lem-coef-finite-closed-shriek, lem-coef-finite-dualizing, thm-coef-finite-hom, cor-coef-finite-verdier]. Frobenius here means the scheme isomorphism $\operatorname{id}_{X_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ on a geometric fiber $X_0\times_{k_0}k$, for the automorphism $\gamma$ of $k$ [def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius], with its corresponding base isomorphism; it is not a claim that the absolute Frobenius of an arbitrary scheme is an isomorphism.

proof.text: The restriction of $|\cdot|_L$ to $E$ equals $|\cdot|_E$ by uniqueness [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-absolute-value]; hence $\mathcal O_E=E\cap\mathcal O_L$ and $0<|\varpi_E|_L<1$. Apply the uniformizer factorization in [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr] in $L$: $\varpi_E=u\varpi_L^e$ for a unit $u$ and a positive integer $e$, the ramification index. Consequently $\varpi_E^n\mathcal O_L=\varpi_L^{en}\mathcal O_L$ for all $n$. The quotient $\mathcal O_L/\varpi_E\mathcal O_L$ is finite by [lem-weil-valued-dvr-finite-quotients] at exponent $e$ in $L$. It is therefore a finitely generated module over $\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E$: the images of all its finitely many elements are a generating set.

The ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ is $(\varpi_E)$-adically complete. Indeed, for a compatible sequence of residues choose lifts $x_n\in R$; then $x_{n+1}-x_n\in\varpi_E^nR$, so $(x_n)$ is Cauchy and converges by [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-complete]. Its limit is in $R$ and has the prescribed residues because $\varpi_E^nR=\{x:|x|_E\le |\varpi_E|_E^n\}$ is closed. The intersection of these balls is zero, so the lift is unique, proving the definition [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. If $y\in\bigcap_n\varpi_E^n\mathcal O_L$, then $|y|_L\le |\varpi_E|_L^n$ for every $n$. Since $0<|\varpi_E|_L<1$, this forces $|y|_L=0$, hence $y=0$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-complete-ring] to $R$, $I=(\varpi_E)$ and $M=\mathcal O_L$ using the finite residue module of step 1. Thus $\mathcal O_L$ is finite over $R$. It is torsion-free since it is a subring of the field $L$ and $R\hookrightarrow L$ is injective; $R$ is a DVR by [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr]. Hence [lem-sc-dvr-fg-torsionfree-free] gives an $R$-basis $b_1,\ldots,b_r$ of $\mathcal O_L$. Reducing this basis gives $B\cong A^{\oplus r}$ as $A$-modules.

source.place: Tag 031D, lemma-finite-over-complete-ring; application after the explicit completeness check

proof.text: On either coefficient site write $T_W=-\otimes_A B_W$ and $U_W$ for restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction] to the identity topos and $A_W\to B_W$: $T_W\dashv U_W$. By [lem-pur-change-of-rings-tensor-comparison] and the basis in step 2, $U_WT_WN\cong N^{\oplus r}$. Thus $T_W$ is exact; $U_W$ is exact and reflects zero objects because it leaves the underlying abelian sheaf unchanged. The exact functors descend termwise by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. The termwise unit and counit of [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy] descend as well and retain their triangle identities, so $T_W\dashv U_W$ also on derived categories, and $U_W$ reflects isomorphisms (apply it to the cohomology of a cone). The exact derived $T_W$ is the derived change of rings of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Tensor extension preserves bounded constructibility: it is exact, and on each stratum a finite locally constant $A$-module becomes a finite locally constant $B$-module. It preserves any Tor interval $[a,b]$ because $(T_WK)\otimes_B^L N\cong K\otimes_A^L U_WN$, on K-flat tensor complexes [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]: the balanced maps are $(p\otimes b)\otimes n\mapsto p\otimes bn$ and $p\otimes n\mapsto(p\otimes1)\otimes n$. They are inverse chain maps; extension of a K-flat $A$-complex is K-flat over $B$, since this formula identifies its tensor with an acyclic $B$-complex with tensor against that complex restricted to $A$, which is acyclic because $U$ is exact.

source.place: Tag 03CZ, lemma-adjointness-tensor-restrict; exact finite-free specialization and passage to complexes

proof.text: First work etale. For a $B$-complex $N$ the canonical comparison $U_XRf_{*,B}N\cong Rf_{*,A}U_TN$ is [lem-sbc-canonical-restrict-scalars-functor-comparisons] on bounded-below objects. For a finite-free extension the same comparison is available on unbounded objects directly: a $B$-K-injective resolution remains $A$-K-injective by [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective], since $T_T$ is exact, and direct image commutes sectionwise with $U$. Under this identification the underlying map of the projection comparison $c_f:T_XRf_{*,A}K\to Rf_{*,B}T_TK$ [def-kun-projection-formula-map] is the finite-sum comparison $(Rf_{*,A}K)^{\oplus r}\to Rf_{*,A}(K^{\oplus r})$. To verify the map, precompose with its $j$-th summand: the projection map is adjoint to the inverse-image counit, and the component is $Rf_*$ applied to the inclusion $k\mapsto k\otimes b_j$; these are exactly the finite-sum inclusions. Any additive functor $F$ preserves this finite sum explicitly: applying $F$ to projections $p_j$ and inclusions $s_j$ preserves $p_js_h=\delta_{jh}$ and $\sum_js_jp_j=1$, giving inverse comparison matrices. Apply this to $Rf_{*,A}$. Thus $U_Xc_f$, and hence $c_f$, is invertible. This proves the first displayed comparison without any cohomological-dimension hypothesis.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: finite-free direct-image case (with the finite-sum calculation written out)

proof.text: For compact supports, factor the chosen morphism as an open immersion followed by a proper morphism. A separated finite-type morphism between our schemes is compactifiable by [thm-nagata-compactification], and the schemes in the compactification are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]: a field has only the zero and unit ideals, so $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian, and each scheme here is finite type over it. For a fixed $f:T\xrightarrow{j}\overline T\xrightarrow{p}X$ with $\overline T$ finite type over $X$, the etale functor is $F_A=Rp_{*,A}j_!$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support]. Extension by zero commutes with coefficient extension and restriction: off the open its stalk is zero, and on the open it is the given stalk [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-stalks, lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative]; the comparison is the map induced by $m\otimes b\mapsto m\otimes b$. Combining this with step 4 for $p$ gives $c^!_f:T_XF_A\xrightarrow{\sim}F_BT_T$, natural in all objects. After restriction it is the finite-sum comparison, whose components are $F_A$ of the inclusions $m\mapsto m\otimes b_j$. This construction also applies to the structure morphism $a_X$.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: counit-defined dualizing comparison; compact-support finite-free calculation

proof.text:
Apply extension and restriction of scalars to the two exceptional adjunctions. Let $F_A\dashv G_A$ and $F_B\dashv G_B$ be either $i_*\dashv Ri^!$ [lem-exc-closed-ambient], or $Ra_{X!}\dashv a_X^{\times}$ [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. Their left functors have the comparison $c:T F_A\xrightarrow{\sim}F_BT$ of steps 4 and 5 (for $i_*$ use its derived direct image). For a $B$-object $N$ and an $A$-test object $P$, the successive adjunctions give
$$\operatorname{Hom}_A(P,UG_BN)=\operatorname{Hom}_B(TP,G_BN)=\operatorname{Hom}_B(F_BTP,N)=\operatorname{Hom}_B(TF_AP,N)=\operatorname{Hom}_A(F_AP,UN)=\operatorname{Hom}_A(P,G_AUN).$$
The bijections are natural in $P,N$; they therefore identify $UG_BN$ with $G_AUN$: evaluate the bijection and its inverse at identity maps to obtain inverse morphisms. Define $b_M:TG_AM\to G_BTM$ to be adjoint to $(T\varepsilon_{A,M})c_{G_AM}^{-1}$. Under the preceding identification and $UTM=M^{\oplus r}$, $Ub_M$ is the map $(G_AM)^{\oplus r}\to G_A(M^{\oplus r})$ whose $j$-th component is $G_A$ of the $j$-th inclusion; this follows by transposing that component, which gives precisely $\varepsilon_{A,M}$ followed by that inclusion. The finite-sum matrix calculation of step 4 makes this an isomorphism. Since $U$ reflects isomorphisms, $b_M$ is an isomorphism. The two choices of $F,G$ give the closed-exceptional comparison and, at $M=A_s$, the dualizing comparison $u:T\omega_{X,A}\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{X,B}$. By definition they obey $\varepsilon_{B,TM}F_B(b_M)=(T\varepsilon_{A,M})c_{G_AM}^{-1}$, which is the required counit identity.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: exceptional and dualizing maps defined by their counits; explicit finite-free adjunction argument

proof.text: The derived tensor--Hom adjunction is the composite $$\operatorname{Hom}(L,H_A(K,N))\cong H^0(\mathcal C,H_A(L,H_A(K,N)))\cong H^0(\mathcal C,H_A(L\otimes_A^LK,N))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(L\otimes_A^LK,N),$$ using [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections] and [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction]. Its counit is evaluation, so the comparison $v_{K,M}$ is the transpose of scalar-extended evaluation pairing.

source.place: Tag 08BJ, lemma-adjoint-preserve-K-injectives; combined with sites-modules Tag 03CZ and the displayed Hom-complex calculation

proof.text: For the finite-free constant ring extension of step 2, [lem-sf-ringed-finite-free-hom-base-change] gives an isomorphism $$T H_A(K,M)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_B(TK,TM)$$ whose defining transpose is exactly the evaluation pairing from the preceding step. Therefore this isomorphism is the map $v_{K,M}$, and it requires no perfectness hypothesis on $K$.

source.place: Tag 08BJ, lemma-adjoint-preserve-K-injectives; combined with sites-modules Tag 03CZ and the displayed Hom-complex calculation

proof.text:
Define $\beta_K$ as $v_{K,\omega_{X,A}}$ followed by $R\mathcal Hom_B(TK,u)$. Steps 6 and 8 make it an isomorphism $TD_{X,A}K\to D_{X,B}TK$. Its evaluation identity is
$$u\,T(\mathrm{ev}_{A,K})=\mathrm{ev}_{B,TK}(\beta_K\otimes1),$$
where tensor reassociation is understood. Indeed, both sides send a functional tensored with $k$ and coefficient $b$ to its value multiplied by $b$, followed by $u$; this is exactly the defining transposition in step 7. The double-dual map is the transpose of evaluation [lem-weil-duality-pairing], so transposing this identity once more gives
$$\beta_{D_AK}\,T(\delta_{A,K})=D_B(\beta_K)\,\delta_{B,TK}.$$
This is the double-dual compatibility (both sides land in $D_B(TD_AK)$). In particular, it does not presume biduality in order to prove compatibility.

source.place: Proof, second and third paragraphs: evaluation and the double-dual transpose

proof.text: The basis was used only to test invertibility. All five maps were defined before choosing a basis by projection, counit or evaluation. For $E\subset L\subset H$, put $d=e(H/L)$ and $C=\mathcal O_H/\varpi_E^n\mathcal O_H=A_{H,den}$. The factorization $\varpi_E=u\varpi_L^e$ and $\varpi_L=v\varpi_H^d$ gives $\varpi_E=uv^e\varpi_H^{de}$ with a unit coefficient, so the iterated coefficient stage is exactly $C$. Compare the maps for $A\to B\to C$ with that for $A\to C$, using $(K\otimes_A B)\otimes_B C\cong K\otimes_A C$. This reassociation and its action on morphisms can be checked on K-flat tensor complexes [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. For direct image, under the inverse-image adjunction both composite maps have transpose $f^*Rf_*K\otimes_A C\to K\otimes_A C$, the inverse-image counit tensored with $C$. For exceptional and dualizing maps, their transposes are respectively $F_C(T_{A,C}G_AM)\xrightarrow{(c_{A,C})^{-1}}T_{A,C}F_AG_AM\xrightarrow{T_{A,C}\varepsilon_A}T_{A,C}M$; expanding either composite gives this formula, since the intermediate $F_B\dashv G_B$ unit followed by counit cancels by its triangle identity. For internal Hom the transpose of either composite is $T_{A,C}(\mathrm{ev}_A)$ after tensor reassociation. Adjunction is a bijection on morphisms, so equality of these displayed transposes proves each composition law, and composition proves the Verdier law. For the identity extension the same transposes are the original counit/evaluation, giving the identity comparisons.

source.place: Proof, third paragraph: transposes for identity and successive field extensions

proof.text: Write $A_n=A_{E,n}$, $B_n=A_{L,en}$ and similarly $A_m,B_m$, with $1\le m\le n$. Since $B_n$ is free over $A_n$ by step 2, $$B_n\otimes^L_{A_n}A_m=B_n/\varpi_E^mB_n=B_m.$$ The K-flat reassociation of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] identifies both iterated scalar extensions in the reduction square with tensoring directly to $B_m$; the balanced map is $(p\otimes a)\otimes b\mapsto p\otimes ab$.

source.place: Proof, third paragraph: quotient followed by extension, with the actual coefficient square and transposes

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-finite-direct-image], [lem-coef-finite-closed-shriek], [lem-coef-finite-dualizing], [thm-coef-finite-hom] and [cor-coef-finite-verdier] to the same-field quotient maps $(A_n\to A_m)$ and $(B_n\to B_m)$. Step 3 supplies finite-Tor constructibility after extension to $B_n$, and $en\ge em\ge1$, so all five comparisons have the required inputs and outputs. The closed-exceptional comparison is first obtained on the pro-etale realization.

source.place: Proof, third paragraph: quotient followed by extension, with the actual coefficient square and transposes

proof.text: The coefficient-reduction squares for direct image, closed exceptional image, and the dualizing object commute by the mate-pasting identities [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting]. Their mates are respectively the direct-image counit, the exceptional counit, and the compact-support counit tensored to $B_m$; intermediate unit/counit pairs cancel by the triangle identities. The finite-Tor hypotheses for dualizing inputs are supplied by [lem-weil-verdier-preservation-strata].

source.place: Proof, third paragraph: quotient followed by extension, with the actual coefficient square and transposes

proof.text: The constant rank-one complexes $A_X$ and $B_X$ are finite-Tor constructible, and their duals are $\omega_{X,A}$ and $\omega_{X,B}$. Hence [lem-weil-verdier-preservation-strata] gives finite-Tor constructibility for these dualizing objects and every dual input in the quotient comparisons.

source.place: Proof, third paragraph: quotient followed by extension, with the actual coefficient square and transposes

proof.text: For internal Hom use [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] on the tensor–Hom adjunction from step 7. Tensor reassociation identifies the pasted left squares; both right mates have transpose evaluation tensored to $B_m$. [thm-coef-finite-hom] identifies the quotient maps with precisely these evaluation transposes at $(n,m)$ over $E$ and $(en,em)$ over $L$. Thus the internal-Hom reduction square commutes. Composing it with the dualizing square gives the Verdier square [cor-coef-finite-verdier]. The evaluation identity and its double-dual transpose from step 9 persist after derived tensor; [lem-weil-verdier-preservation-strata] verifies finite-Tor constructibility for the dual inputs in these quotient comparisons.

source.place: Proof, third paragraph: quotient followed by extension, with the actual coefficient square and transposes

proof.text:
These comparisons give the finite-coefficient pro-étale assertions. Direct image commutes with comparison pullback by [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate]: $f$ is qcqs and its input bounded below. Tensor pullback commutes with derived tensor by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. The exceptional functor is the transported étale functor [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. The dualizing and internal-Hom identifications, including evaluation and double-dual, are [lem-weil-finite-duality-site-comparison] at each finite coefficient stage: its first input is finite-Tor, its second bounded constructible, including the dualizing objects established above.
To identify the maps, paste the site-comparison and coefficient squares using [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting]. The canonical-mate counit normalization identifies the pulled-back inverse-image counit with the pro-étale counit. After tensor comparison the pulled-back projection transpose is therefore that counit tensored with $B$. For internal Hom the transpose is pulled-back evaluation; for the exceptional map it is the transported étale exceptional counit. Consequently these are the named coefficient maps on the pro-étale realization, and the functor carries all previously proved map identities to it.

source.place: Proof, all paragraphs: finite constructible realization on the two sites

proof.text: The remaining recovery of the étale closed-exceptional quotient map is [lem-coef-finite-etale-descent], applied over $E$ at $(n,m)$ and over $L$ at $(en,em)$. Its input is finite-Tor constructible on the étale site by the hypotheses and step 3. It places both étale outputs in the same finite-Tor constructible category and identifies its pulled-back counit-defined map with [lem-coef-finite-closed-shriek]. Its faithfulness clause then descends the pro-étale mixed reduction square just proved. Thus this use of the pro-étale closed coefficient theorem recovers exactly the étale map and square, with their required output typing.

source.place: Proof, all paragraphs: finite constructible realization on the two sites

proof.text: Finally, transport a diagram along scheme isomorphisms (and the base isomorphism when present). The induced site equivalences identify module sheaves by inverse reindexing; their inverse transports are actual inverses up to the canonical pullback identifications. The formula for tensor, scalar extension, the Hom differential, and evaluation is unchanged under this reindexing. Transport the left adjunction and its unit/counit as well. The transported right adjoint is the original right adjoint under the unique counit-compatible identification; after bringing both functors into the same categories this uniqueness is [lem-trf-adjoint-mate]. Consequently the transported comparison is the comparison on the transported diagram: both have exactly the projection-counit or evaluation transposes displayed in steps 4, 6, 7 and 9. This includes the semilinear Frobenius isomorphism of [def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius] because $\gamma$ is a field automorphism with inverse. Lastly $e\ge1$ and for every $m\ge1$ there is $n\ge1$ with $en\ge m$ (take $n=m$); the set of such $n$ is a nonempty tail and hence directed. Thus the indices $en$ are cofinal for the inverse tower. The ideal equality in step 1 identifies exactly those levels with $B_n$; changing either uniformizer by a unit does not change these ideals or quotient maps.

source.place: Proof, final paragraph: scheme-isomorphism naturality, Frobenius transport, and cofinal levels

The former internal-Hom step is split into the tensor--Hom transpose (step 7) and the existing finite-free change-of-rings theorem lem-sf-ringed-finite-free-hom-base-change (step 8). The former coefficient-reduction step is split into tensor reassociation (step 11), applications of the five existing quotient comparisons (step 12) and mate pasting (step 13). The former constructibility/map step is split into finite-Tor typing (step 14) and the internal-Hom/Verdier mate argument (step 15). One new node, lem-coef-finite-etale-descent, states the etale recovery of the closed-exceptional quotient comparison used in step 17. Maintainer review (2026-10-17) removed a verbatim-duplicate internal-Hom mate step and corrected three step cross-references; all proof steps are under 2000 characters.
